evidence_refs: The old model's global least-squares fit has fit RMSE 0.2549 and dev RMSE 0.8752, so dependence on only u and h is inadequate.
At matched u=0.4 and h=0.3, dev means are about 1.313 for all-positive history and -0.721 for all-negative history, showing a large history effect.
At matched u=0.65 and h=0.5, observed_A means are about 0.644 for [1,0,0,0] and 0.941 for [0,0,0,1]; equal sums can yield different responses, so history placement matters.

The prior proposal was rejected because exp requires a dimensionless input; times/tau has time exponent zero and is dimensionless, but the proposed expression's dt factor gives the summed memory time units. The revised quantity omits dt because all supplied intervals have fixed dt=1 s.

experiments.purpose: Measure oldest-pulse response at a new drive, paired with the newest-pulse condition to test temporal placement.
Measure newest-pulse response at the same drive and wait; compare with the oldest-pulse condition.
Repeat the oldest-pulse condition after a longer wait to test whether its contribution changes with waiting time.
Repeat the newest-pulse condition after a longer wait, separating waiting-time effects from pulse-age effects.

measurement_requests: Collect four repeats per condition and report raw responses; retain the calibrated reference-channel error bound of 0.015 response units.

quantities.interpretation: Dimensionless exponentially age-weighted summary of prior drive. Since each interval has dt=1 s, the fixed interval duration is omitted; times/tau is dimensionless. This is a candidate history representation, not a complete response law.
quantities.name: memory

scaffold.rationale: The matched-history contrasts establish that u and h alone omit relevant history information, while the isolated-pulse contrast shows that an unweighted sum cannot distinguish temporal placement. The all-positive history responses also vary with h, motivating a representation that discounts older input as time passes. The previous attempt failed dimensional validation because tau was declared dimensionless and the integral included dt, yielding a time-valued sum. This revision assigns tau time units and omits the fixed 1 s interval factor, leaving memory dimensionless and making exp(times/tau) valid. It is intentionally partial: no response coefficients or final response law are supplied. The four paired conditions vary pulse age and wait at a new controlled drive to test this representation.

predicted_contrasts: At fixed u and h, different histories predict different responses through memory; for positive tau, a newest isolated pulse has greater memory weight than an oldest isolated pulse.
For the same history and u, increasing h shifts the supplied negative times older relative to the response and reduces memory; the response change combines this with the explicit wait_gain*h term.
At fixed u and history, changing h tests whether the direct waiting-time effect and the wait-induced decay of memory are both needed.
annotation.scientific_change: Completes the history representation as a shared response law with an offset and separate drive, waiting-time, and memory coefficients. The large matched-u,h contrast between all-positive and all-negative histories motivates a history term; the contrast between equal-sum oldest and newest pulse histories motivates temporal weighting. The proposed paired pulse conditions vary pulse placement and waiting time to test those predictions. All four coefficients must be declared as shared response-unit parameters with finite bounds and initial values in a build step before fitting; they are not present in the fixed partial construction, so this expression is not currently fit-ready.
